questions.prompt: A scheduler restarts a finished job because it never received the success signal. What property of the job makes the restart harmless?
options: Idempotence: the job detects completed outputs and does not redo or corrupt them
A large backoffLimit, so the scheduler keeps retrying until the run succeeds
Running with parallelism 1, so two copies of the job never overlap
Using the latest image tag, so each restart picks up the newest fixes
questions.explanation: At-least-once scheduling is made safe by idempotent jobs that check for a completion marker.

questions.prompt: backoff_delays(6, base=2, cap=30): what is the sum of all six delays in seconds?
Checkpoints cost C = 5 s and the mean time between failures is M = 7200 s. What checkpoint interval T = sqrt(2CM) in seconds (one decimal)?
In which order should a job publish its outputs?
options: Result files atomically, then the DONE marker last
Both at the same time in the same file handle
DONE marker first, then result files
Order does not matter if the filesystem is local
questions.explanation: DONE must imply that all outputs are complete, so it is written last.

questions.prompt: Why is docker pull exp:latest a poor basis for reproducing an old result?
options: latest always points at the oldest build in the repository
Docker cannot pull a tag, only a digest, so the command fails
latest is a movable tag, so the bytes behind it can change
Tags are encrypted, so the image contents cannot be inspected
questions.explanation: Tags are pointers; only a digest identifies exact image content.

questions.prompt: A job has 200 steps of 3 s. It is killed right after step 130 completes and the last checkpoint was after step 125. How many seconds of work are redone?
Design the output contract for a sweep of 144 runs on 4 preemptible machines: directory layout, completion marker, what is recorded for reproducibility, and how a rerun avoids repeated work.
rubric: Output directory derived from a canonical config hash, with result files, a manifest of checksums and a DONE marker written last.
Records commit and image digest (and seeds/dataset version) with each run.
Rerun skips runs with valid DONE/manifest, resumes others from checkpoints, and uses atomic writes.
